subject: atlas
summary: Atlas renders weather frames ahead of time and serves them as files that never change. That one choice sets the rest: a scheduled worker that writes, a small read-only API, and a CDN in front of both.

items: No accounts and no personal data: nothing to protect per user, everything cacheable.
Traffic follows the weather: quiet for weeks, then ten times normal for a day.
The source data arrives hourly, so nothing needs to be fresher than that.
A small team: managed services over servers to patch.

rows: Newest frame at most 70 minutes old
Hourly ingest; an alarm on the age of the current run
A frame in under 200 ms, 95th percentile
Unchanging files on the CDN; a cache hit needs no origin
The map loads 99.9% of the month
Cached frames survive an API or ingest outage
Flat when idle, linear on storm days
Lambda and the CDN bill per request; ingest is one task an hour

items.title: Render frames on a schedule, never per request
items.decision: The Ingest Worker draws every frame once per model run.
items.why: Rendering is heavy and the data changes hourly, so work per request would buy nothing.
items.alternatives: A tile server that renders on demand.

items.title: Run-stamped keys that never change
items.decision: Each run writes under its own prefix; the catalog points at the current one.
items.why: No cache invalidation, and rolling back is one pointer change.
items.alternatives: Overwriting fixed keys and purging the CDN.

items.title: Ingest beside the source
items.decision: Run in the same region as NOAA's public buckets.
items.why: The download is the largest transfer in the system; a same-region read is fast and carries no transfer charge.
items.alternatives: The region closest to most viewers.

items.title: Fargate for ingest, Lambda for the API
items.decision: A container task for the hourly render; functions for requests.
items.why: The render is long and memory-heavy; requests are short and arrive in bursts.

blocks.text: Seven containers and three external systems. Only the Ingest Worker writes.
Two environments, staging and production, each an account of its own, created from the same infrastructure code.

rows: No user data. The bucket is private and only the CDN reads it. Each role may touch only its own resources.
Structured logs, one dashboard, alarms on run age, API errors and ingest failures.
Environment variables set by infrastructure code. No secrets: every upstream is public.
Frames expire after 48 hours; catalog items carry a time-to-live.
